subject: Chemistry
title: Same Face, Different Inside: The Lanthanoids
summary: The lanthanoids (lanthanum and the fourteen elements after it) have the general configuration [Xe] 4f¹⁻¹⁴ 5d⁰⁻¹ 6s². Each new electron goes into the deep 4f subshell, shielded by 5s²5p⁶, while the outer 6s² stays the same, so the elements are very alike (the Ytterby minerals took chemists over a century to sort out). Losing 6s² and one more electron gives the characteristic +3 state (La³⁺ 4f⁰ … Lu³⁺ 4f¹⁴). +4 and +2 appear near empty, half-filled or full 4f (Ce⁴⁺ 4f⁰, Tb⁴⁺ 4f⁷, Eu²⁺ 4f⁷, Yb²⁺ 4f¹⁴), but Ce⁴⁺ is a strong oxidant and Eu²⁺ a strong reductant: both return to +3.

notes.title: 17 – The Lanthanoids: Electronic Configuration and Oxidation States

keyPoints: **Lanthanoids**: La and the 14 elements after it; a separate row of the periodic table.
**[Xe] 4f¹⁻¹⁴ 5d⁰⁻¹ 6s²**: new electrons go into the **deep 4f**; the outer 6s² is the same, so they are very alike.
**+3** is characteristic: lose 6s² + one more (La³⁺ 4f⁰ … Lu³⁺ 4f¹⁴).
**+4 / +2** near 4f⁰, 4f⁷, 4f¹⁴ (Ce⁴⁺, Tb⁴⁺, Eu²⁺, Yb²⁺); Ce⁴⁺ oxidant, Eu²⁺ reductant: back to +3.

blocks.p: Pr = [Xe]4f³6s². Pr³⁺ loses 6s² and one 4f electron: [Xe]4f². Tb = [Xe]4f⁹6s²; Tb⁴⁺ loses 6s² and two 4f electrons: [Xe]4f⁷ (half-filled).
